event_description: Tehran: Gandhi Hospital (damaged by nearby strike on state TV tower, Mar 2 — IVF department destroyed)

Iranian civilian death toll estimated at 400+: Iranian Red Crescent and state media report over 400 civilian deaths from US and Israeli strikes in the first week. Independent verification is impossible due to media access restrictions. Iran claims the number is significantly higher. Pentagon states all targets are military or dual-use and that civilian casualties are 'deeply regretted but not the objective.'

Iranian infrastructure damage assessment — power, water, fuel: The ICRC reports significant damage to Iranian civilian infrastructure including power generation (30-40% of national grid offline in western Iran), water treatment disruption in Ahvaz and Kermanshah, and fuel shortages as refinery capacity is degraded. Hospitals are operating on backup generators. Iran's road and rail network is severely disrupted by strikes on bridges and logistics hubs.

Iranian state media claims hospital hit in Ahvaz: Iranian state television broadcasts footage of a damaged hospital in Ahvaz, claiming a US airstrike struck the facility, killing 12 patients and staff. Pentagon states the target was an IRGC logistics hub 400 meters away and that the hospital damage was caused by secondary explosions. Independent verification not yet possible.

Iran Health Ministry: 1,444 killed, 18,551 injured: Iranian Health Ministry releases updated casualty figures: 1,444 killed and 18,551 injured since February 28. Separately, Hengaw (Kurdish human rights organization) reports 4,400+ Iranian military personnel killed, a significantly higher figure. Iranian Red Crescent reports 20,000+ civilian buildings affected including 16,000 residential units. 31 major hospitals damaged, 12 rendered inactive. WHO has verified 13 attacks on healthcare infrastructure in Iran.

Lebanese casualties reach 826+ killed — IDF ground operations continue: Lebanese Health Ministry reports cumulative death toll from Israeli strikes and ground operations has reached 826+ killed and 2,009+ wounded since March 2. At least 102 children among the dead. 850,000+ displaced. IDF ground operations in southern Lebanon continue with heavy fighting around Bint Jbeil and the eastern sector. Hezbollah's Radwan Force continues to employ IEDs, tunnel systems, and anti-tank missiles against advancing IDF forces.

Hengaw 5th report: 5,300 killed in 18 days — 511 civilians — 120 children: Hengaw Organization's 5th report documents 5,300 killed in the first 18 days of the war — 511 civilians (9.6%), including 120 minors and 160 women, plus 4,800+ military personnel. Strikes recorded in 178 cities across 25 provinces. Iran Health Ministry separately reports 1,444 killed and 18,551 injured. HRANA documented 3,114 deaths. US: 13 KIA, ~200 wounded.

Mass casualty event declared at Soroka Hospital, Beersheba. IAEA: no abnormal radiation detected. Iran's Ghalibaf: 'If the Israeli regime is unable to intercept missiles in the heavily protected Dimona area, it is operationally a sign of entering a new phase of the battle.'

event_description: ICRC: 'civilians bearing the brunt' — Philippines declares state of emergency: ICRC President Mirjana Spoljaric Egger stated 'civilians are bearing the brunt' and called attacks on civilian infrastructure 'unacceptable.' Up to 3.2 million Iranians are internally displaced. 830,000 Lebanese displaced (20% of population). 25 hospitals damaged in Iran, 9 out of service. 42,000+ civilian sites damaged. IFRC launched CHF 40 million emergency appeal for Iran. The Philippines declared a state of emergency over the energy crisis with fuel prices more than doubled and nationwide protests in Manila.

Humanitarian toll approaches 3,000 killed — Iran agrees to facilitate aid through Hormuz: Iranian casualties range from 1,750 (Iran deputy UN rep) to 3,114 (HRANA) with dramatic discrepancies. HRANA documented 3,114 deaths by March 17 (1,354 civilians, 1,138 military, 622 unclassified). 217 children killed per HRANA. WHO reports 13+ hospitals/health facilities attacked, 6 evacuated. OCHA: 6,668+ civilian structures targeted. Minab school (Feb 28) killed 150-170+ (mostly schoolchildren) — UN investigating as potential war crime. In a breakthrough, Iran agreed March 27 to 'facilitate and expedite' humanitarian aid through Strait of Hormuz.

IDF strikes ~170 Hezbollah sites — 800+ Hezbollah killed — 3 journalists and 9 paramedics killed: IDF struck approximately 170 Hezbollah sites over the weekend, claiming 800+ Hezbollah operatives killed including hundreds from the elite Radwan Force. 2 Israeli soldiers were seriously wounded and 7 moderately wounded in southern Lebanon clashes. Hezbollah fired 5 rockets at Galilee. Earlier in the week, Hezbollah launched 600 rockets/missiles/drones in a single 24-hour period. 3 journalists were killed in Israeli strikes in Jezzine, including Al Manar TV's Ali Shuaib. 9 paramedics were killed on March 28 alone. Lebanese cumulative: 1,189 killed (124 children, 42 health workers), 3,229 injured, ~1 million displaced.

Iran strikes chemical plant, Haifa refinery, Kuwait water plant: Iran struck a chemical plant in Ne'ot Hovav (Israel), an oil refinery in Haifa, and a water/electrical plant in Kuwait. Iranian Navy Commander Shahram Irani directly threatened USS Abraham Lincoln, vowing to launch 'various types of sea-to-sea missiles' once the carrier enters firing range.

Israeli airstrike on Beirut's Jnah neighborhood kills 7: An Israeli airstrike without warning on Beirut's Jnah neighborhood killed 7 people and wounded 26, per the Lebanese Health Ministry's final count. In a separate naval strike on Beirut, Israel killed Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem, commander of Hezbollah's Southern Front — described by the IDF as the most senior Hezbollah figure eliminated, with '40+ years of experience.' A second 'senior terrorist' killed in separate Beirut strike.

event_description: IRGC cluster bomb missile strikes Bnei Brak — children critically wounded: The first wave of three Iranian ballistic missile salvos carried a cluster bomb warhead that struck Bnei Brak, east of Tel Aviv, spreading submunitions over a residential area. 14-16 people wounded including a 10-12-year-old girl critically injured by glass shrapnel in her bed (Sheba Medical Center: 'teams fighting for her life'), a 13-year-old boy seriously wounded while trying to wake his deaf mother (both unable to reach shelter), and the girl's father in moderate condition. Second and third volleys largely intercepted; a fourth salvo of two missiles toward central Israel also defeated.

IDF reframes Lebanon war goals — disarming Hezbollah 'unrealistic' without full occupation: On April 3, the IDF reframed its war goals in Lebanon, acknowledging that militarily disarming Hezbollah is 'unrealistic' without occupying all of Lebanon. Lebanon death toll: 1,345+ killed, 3,935 injured, ~1 million displaced (20% of population). 200,000+ have crossed into Syria. The Lebanese government took the unprecedented step of proscribing Hezbollah's military activities. 132,000+ in 620+ collective shelters at 94% capacity. 49 primary healthcare centers and 5 hospitals shut.

18 civilians including 2 children killed in US-Israeli attack on Alborz Province: At least 18 civilians including 2 children killed in US-Israeli attack on Iran's Alborz Province overnight April 6-7. Tehran residential areas also struck with Red Crescent rescue workers responding to collapsed buildings. Six children (4 girls, 2 boys under age 10) killed in overnight strikes on Tehran residential area.

Iran calls for human shields at power plants — WHO reports 307 health facilities damaged: Iran's Deputy Sports Minister Alireza Rahimi called on young people, artists, athletes, and students to form 'human chains' around power plants at 2:00 PM local time Tuesday. A Revolutionary Guard general urged parents to send children to man checkpoints. WHO has verified 20+ attacks on healthcare in Iran resulting in at least 9 deaths. Iranian Red Crescent reports 307 health/medical/emergency facilities damaged. UNHCR: up to 3.2 million Iranians temporarily displaced. Iran's internet connectivity at 4% of normal. HRANA: 3,540-3,546 killed (nearly double Health Ministry's 2,076).

audit_note: Strike-tempo report; health terms appear in an appended situation note
event_description: Israel conducts 50+ strikes in Lebanon in 24 hours — reduced Beirut targeting under US pressure: By April 10, Israel had conducted 50+ additional strikes in Lebanon in 24 hours. Al Jazeera's correspondent noted a marked reduction in Beirut-area targeting, attributed to direct US pressure. Trump told NBC he asked Netanyahu to be 'a little more low-key' in Lebanon to protect the Iran negotiations. IDF has 5 divisions operating in southern Lebanon and has systematically destroyed all main bridges over the Litani River. WHO warned Lebanese hospitals may exhaust vital medical supplies within days. UNICEF reports 600 children killed or injured since the start of Lebanon operations.

Trump announces US naval BLOCKADE of Strait of Hormuz: Following the talks' collapse, Trump posted on Truth Social: 'Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz.' He ordered the Navy to 'seek and interdict every vessel in International Waters that has paid a toll to Iran,' to destroy Iranian mines, and threatened: 'Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!' He warned: 'At an appropriate moment, we are fully LOCKED AND LOADED, and our Military will finish up the little that is left of Iran!' Axios reports Trump had been discussing the blockade option for days as a contingency. This represents a strategic flip — taking Iran's leverage card by denying all Strait access under US naval control. Key complication: Iran reportedly lost track of mines it planted. Another: Chinese, Indian, and Pakistani ships have been among the few transiting under deals with Tehran.

IDF captures Bint Jbeil — 100+ Hezbollah killed — Red Cross paramedic killed by drone: The IDF reports it is close to capturing Bint Jbeil, Hezbollah's historic stronghold, with 100+ Hezbollah operatives killed in the battle. Sirens sounded across the Galilee for Hezbollah drone attacks including near Acre — IDF shot down several drones. A Lebanese Red Cross paramedic was killed by an Israeli drone that 'directly targeted' the team (NBC News). April 12 saw Hezbollah launch ~20 rockets at northern Israel plus drone attacks on Kfar Yuval, Yir'on, and Kiryat Shmona (1:20 AM barrage); the IDF raided Bint Jbeil Governmental Hospital, killing ~20 Hezbollah operatives. Netanyahu visited southern Lebanon with Defense Minister Katz and IDF Chief Zamir, declaring 'the war continues.' Katz announced Operation 'Silver Plough' to demolish homes along the border. Israeli forces rammed UNIFIL vehicles with a Merkava tank on two occasions. Lebanon cumulative (Lebanon Public Health Emergency Operation Center via CGTN): 2,055 killed, 6,588 wounded — up from 2,020/6,436 on Day 44.

Iran casualty figures show nearly 4x spread across sources: Iranian civilian and military casualty figures remain deeply contested. Iran Health Ministry (official): ~2,000+ killed — widely seen as understated. HRANA (U.S.-based NGO) Apr 7: 3,636 total (1,701 civilians, 1,221 military) — named verification. Hengaw (Norway-based) Apr 8: 7,650 total (1,030 civilians, 6,620 military) — field reporting, more than double HRANA driven almost entirely by military casualty estimates. IDF claims 6,000+ IRGC killed. Iran's internet blackout severely limits independent verification. HRANA acknowledges military casualties are 'significantly higher' than its confirmed count. The gap between these figures is a nearly 4x spread. OCHA reports 115,193 civilian units damaged, 763 schools, 334 health/emergency centers as of April 3. The Pasteur Institute was severely damaged. WHO verified 23 attacks on healthcare in Iran. Iran executed at least 14 protesters between Mar 17 and Apr 6 including teen wrestler Saleh Mohammadi and 18-year-old Amir Hossein Hatami (Hengaw).

audit_note: WHO emergency logistics hub suspended - humanitarian access insult, not a facility attack
event_description: Humanitarian access collapsing — WHO Dubai hub ON HOLD: Humanitarian access is collapsing. WHO's Dubai logistics hub — the global health emergency hub — is on hold due to regional insecurity, delaying 50+ emergency supply requests from 25 countries. The Strait of Hormuz closure disrupted 80%+ of GCC food imports. UNHCR has issued an $80 million appeal for 2.8 million affected people in Iran. Iran has 3.2 million+ internally displaced (compounded by severe flooding in 24 provinces). Lebanon's 1.2 million+ displaced represents 14% of the population; 200,000+ have fled into Syria. 55,500 Afghan refugees returned to Afghanistan from Iran. Lebanon infrastructure crisis: Nine bridges over the Litani River have been destroyed, severing southern Lebanon from the north. The sole remaining lifeline — Qasmieh Bridge — serves 71,000+ people in the Tyre area. Fifty primary health care centers and 5 hospitals closed. WHO documented 77 attacks on healthcare in Lebanon with 53 health worker deaths. Food prices spiking: vegetables up 20%+, bread up 17% in one month.

Battle of Bint Jbeil Day 5-6 — IDF 98th Division within 300-400m of stadium: The Battle of Bint Jbeil continued for a fifth-sixth day. The IDF 98th Division approached within 300-400m of the Bint Jbeil stadium — the site of Hassan Nasrallah's famous 2000 'spider's web' speech. An estimated 100+ Hezbollah fighters have been killed in the battle, with dozens remaining active. The IDF raided a hospital where armed Hezbollah operatives were sheltering. Apr 13: 2 IDF soldiers moderately wounded and 6 lightly wounded by a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon. A woman was injured in Nahariya, northern Israel, by a Hezbollah rocket. An ICRC center was struck in Tyre, killing one person. Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem rejected the April 15 Israel-Lebanon talks as 'pointless' and 'a free concession.' Lebanon cumulative toll: 2,089+ killed (+34 from Apr 13), 6,762+ wounded (+174 from Apr 13). IDF forced evacuation orders now cover ~14% of Lebanon's territory (1,470 sq km).

audit_note: Deliberation/threat reporting; no health-system event occurred
event_description: WSJ: Trump considering limited military strikes on Iran as leverage: The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump and his advisers are considering resuming limited military strikes on Iran as leverage for talks. This has NOT been implemented. The blockade itself is viewed by Iran and multiple analysts as a potential ceasefire violation, with the IRGC explicitly stating that any military vessel approaching the Strait of Hormuz constitutes a breach. Trump's April 13 Fox News interview threatened destruction of Iran's 'water, desalination plans, electric-generating plants.' However, the ceasefire on the Iran front has now held for approximately 168 hours with zero confirmed new US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory. The April 11 Lavan Oil Refinery strike remains the most recent alleged violation, with attribution unclear.

Hezbollah launches ~30 rockets at northern Israel — Bint Jbeil nears conclusion: Hezbollah launched approximately 30 rockets at northern Israel on Apr 15 morning (IDF confirmed). Hezbollah claimed 24 separate attacks Apr 14 on northern Israel and IDF positions in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah also shot down an Israeli Hermes 450 drone and fired SAMs at Israeli warplanes. Hezbollah rejected the Apr 14 Washington Israel-Lebanon talks — Secretary-General Naim Qassem called them 'futile' and a 'free concession.' Battle of Bint Jbeil status Apr 14-15: IDF claims near-complete capture with only 'several dozen' Hezbollah fighters remaining; 100+ Hezbollah killed in close-quarters combat and airstrikes since Apr 9 launch; no rockets have been launched from within Bint Jbeil since the offensive began. Apr 14 engagements: 10 IDF paratroopers wounded (3 severely) in clash with Hezbollah cell; 3 Hezbollah fighters killed; 1 IDF soldier killed, 13 total wounded in separate incidents across Lebanon; 3 Radwan Force fighters captured and turned over to Unit 504 interrogation; an armored battalion commander was seriously wounded; IDF Northern Command Chief Maj. Gen. Milo visited for assessment. Apr 15: IDF's 8th Brigade (91st Division) uncovered anti-tank missile launcher aimed at northern Israel, plus weapons caches with anti-tank missiles, explosives, and ammunition; IDF struck a Hezbollah command center. Five IDF divisions operating in southern Lebanon: 36th, 91st, 98th, 146th, 162nd. 'Operation Silver Plough' (announced Apr 13 by DM Katz) is demolishing all border village structures claimed as 'terror outposts.' Haaretz: IDF operating 'using methods similar to those used in Gaza Strip.' Since March 2, Hezbollah has killed at least 12 IDF soldiers and 2 civilians. IDF Home Front Command warned Apr 14 evening that Hezbollah may temporarily increase attacks to influence the Washington negotiations. Lebanon cumulative: 2,089-2,124 killed (EOC/Health Ministry); +43 Lebanese killed in past 24 hrs per manifest.

IDF Nabatieh strike kills 19 incl. 13 Lebanese State Security — Hezbollah hits Ashdod + Nahariya church: An IDF strike on Nabatieh Apr 16 killed 19 people, including 13 Lebanese State Security personnel. Hezbollah struck Ashdod (claimed targeting of Ashdod Naval Base) and damaged a 1,500-year-old church in Nahariya with a missile. Cumulative Hezbollah rocket/UAV activity since Mar 2: 1,121 attack waves (Alma Center). Battle of Bint Jbeil consolidated by IDF 98th Division — 100+ Hezbollah killed cumulatively since Apr 9, 3 surrendered Apr 15. Trump floated an unconfirmed 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire Apr 16 (NBC) — not confirmed by either party. Rubio-Aoun phone call Apr 16 on Lebanon ceasefire. Hezbollah MP Hussein Hajj Hassan condemned the Apr 14 Israel-Lebanon talks as 'a grave sin.' Lebanon MoPH (via WAFA/Al Jazeera) end-Apr 15: 2,167 killed / 7,061 wounded. No kinetic Iranian action Apr 15-16. No Houthi Red Sea shipping attacks in the 48-hour window; Iraqi PMF quiet.

audit_note: UNIFIL peacekeeper fatality; health terms come from an appended MoPH toll citation
event_description: LEBANON TRUCE BREACHED — French UNIFIL CWO killed, 3 wounded; Macron blames Hezbollah: The 10-day Lebanon ceasefire that took effect Thursday midnight Beirut time suffered its first significant breach on April 18. A French chief warrant officer serving with UNIFIL was killed and three French peacekeepers wounded in southern Lebanon — the first allied fatality on the Lebanon front. President Macron posted that 'everything suggests that responsibility for this attack lies with Hezbollah.' Separately, one Lebanese was killed in an Israeli strike on a motorcycle in the south, and earlier MoPH reporting documented one death in Kounine overnight April 17. Netanyahu declared the anti-Hezbollah campaign 'not over' but Trump publicly told Israel it is 'prohibited' from striking Lebanon — 'enough is enough.' Lebanese President Aoun declared Lebanon will no longer be 'an arena for others' wars.' Lebanon MoPH cumulative Apr 17: 2,294 killed, 7,544 wounded, ≥172 children, 100+ paramedics/health workers dead.

Southern Lebanon (UNIFIL AO): Attack on UNIFIL patrol (attribution alleged Hezbollah) — 1 French chief warrant officer (CWO) serving with UNIFIL killed; 3 French peacekeepers wounded. Separately: 1 Lebanese killed in Israeli strike on a motorcycle in the south. Earlier MoPH reporting documented one death in Kounine overnight Apr 17.

audit_note: [lebanon-sunday-apr19] Same incident: Apr 19 Lebanon Sunday toll incl. Red Cross paramedic (Day-51 timeline + Day-52 strike-file rows)
event_description: Lebanon Sunday: ≥35 killed including Red Cross paramedic during 10-day truce: At least 35 people were killed in Lebanon on Sunday, Apr 19, including a Lebanese Red Cross paramedic, according to Lebanese authorities — despite the 10-day Israel-Lebanon ceasefire that took effect ~5:00 PM ET Apr 16. IDF reportedly struck 200+ Hezbollah targets over the weekend Apr 18-19 (UNVERIFIED count). The Battle of Bint Jbeil continues, with IDF's 98th Division claiming 100+ Hezbollah killed cumulatively since the operation began Apr 9, though the town remains contested. Cumulative Lebanese deaths since March 2 now stand at 2,020-2,196+ (Lebanese MoPH mid-April); 177 children killed; 1.2 million displaced. Separately on Apr 18, French UNIFIL Sgt 1st Class Florian Montorio was killed in an ambush, with Macron blaming Hezbollah (Hezbollah denied). Haaretz reported Apr 18 that Netanyahu privately admitted he has 'not succeeded' against Hezbollah.

Iran Legal Medicine Organization: at least 3,375 killed in Iran — 383 children ≤18 — most authoritative official figure: Iran's Legal Medicine Organization (via Mizan; forensic chief Abbas Masjedi), publishing updated April 20 figures, reported at least 3,375 killed in Iran — 2,875 male, 496 female, 383 children ≤18, 4 unidentified. This is now the most authoritative official Iranian count. HRANA (Apr 7) had 3,636 (1,701 civilians, 1,221 military, 714 unclassified). Iran International separately cited 4,700+ security force members. IDF claims 6,000+ IRGC killed. Lebanon MoPH Apr 20 revised its own cumulative toll upward to 2,387 killed and 7,602 wounded since March 2 — an ~8-10% increase over the prior 2,167-2,196 baseline (Wikipedia / Al Jazeera). Children killed in Lebanon: ≥177.

audit_note: Medical-supply cargo seized under blockade - access/supply-chain insult
event_description: Iranian Red Crescent: US-seized cargo ship was carrying 'lifesaving medical supplies': The Iranian Red Crescent issued a statement on Apr 23 claiming that a cargo ship seized earlier in the week by the US was reportedly carrying 'lifesaving medical supplies.' The claim could not be independently verified. CNN separately reported multiple oil spills visible from space following strikes on oil facilities and ships during the broader conflict — an emerging environmental dimension to the Hormuz crisis.

IDF kills 6 Hezbollah in Bint Jbeil; 2 civilians killed in Touline air strike: IDF said it 'eliminated' 6 Hezbollah fighters in Bint Jbeil exchange of fire. Lebanese Health Ministry reported 2 killed in Israeli air strike on Touline; several wounded in Yater artillery strike. IDF struck Hezbollah rocket launchers in Yater and Kafra. Hezbollah announced shootdown of an Israeli drone and an attack on an IDF APC in Ramyah. Netanyahu: Israel maintains 'full freedom of action against any threat.' Total Lebanese toll since Mar 2: 2,491 killed / 7,719 wounded.
Touline, southern Lebanon: IDF airstrike — Lebanese Health Ministry: 2 KILLED in Israeli air strike on the southern town of Touline. Several wounded in separate Israeli artillery attack on Yater.

Israeli strikes kill 4 in Yohmor al-Shaqeef; IDF intercepts 'suspicious aerial target' in south Lebanon: Lebanese Health Ministry reported two Israeli strikes — on a truck and on a motorbike — in Yohmor al-Shaqeef (Nabatieh district) killed four people. The IDF separately confirmed it intercepted a 'suspicious aerial target' in southern Lebanon that 'never crossed into Israeli territory.' These follow the Apr 23 three-week truce extension; Hezbollah has dismissed the extension as 'meaningless.' Cumulative Lebanese MoPH toll Apr 24 stood at 2,491 K / 7,719 W; running total adjusts to 2,495 K with Apr 25 additions.

Lebanon 'Black Wednesday' — 28 killed in southern Lebanon Israeli strikes: Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon killed at least 28 people in 24h, including 2 Lebanese army soldiers, 3 paramedics, and members of two families. Reuters/CNN cited 9 killed Apr 30; Lebanese NNA cited 14; Al Jazeera updated to 28 over 24h.

Israel kills 10-12 in Lebanon strikes despite Apr 17 ceasefire: Israeli airstrikes on Habboush (6 killed incl. woman + child, 8 wounded) and three other southern villages (4 killed) — total 10-12 killed. Hezbollah fired drones/rockets; 2 IDF soldiers lightly wounded near Margaliot. Lebanese MoPH cumulative since Mar 2: 2,618 killed, 8,094 wounded.

Lebanese MoPH: cumulative 2,659 killed / 8,183 wounded since March 2: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health updated cumulative toll: 2,659 killed (+41 in 24h) and 8,183 wounded since outbreak Mar 2. Among May 1–2 deaths confirmed in NNA reports: at least one woman, multiple children injured (Habboush). Over 1M displaced (UN/UNRWA).

location_name: Southern Lebanon (multi-locale: Shoukine, Kfar Dajjal, Lwaizeh, Habboush, Nabatieh, Tyre district)
event_description: Southern Lebanon (multi-locale: Shoukine, Kfar Dajjal, Lwaizeh, Habboush, Nabatieh, Tyre district): Air strike series + drone strikes — 41 killed in 24h per Lebanese MoPH cumulative — Shoukine (3), Kfar Dajjal (2 in car strike), Lwaizeh (3 in home), Shoukin (2), Sammaiyeh / Tyre district (3). IDF: 'approximately 70 military structures and approximately 50 Hezbollah infrastructure sites were dismantled across several areas.'

IDF issues forced-displacement orders for villages NORTH of Litani — first major geographic expansion since 17 Apr Lebanon ceasefire: IDF Arabic-spokesman Avichay Adraee posts evacuation order on X covering 10+ villages, several in Nabatieh District north of the Litani River. Residents told to move 'at least 1,000 metres' into open areas. Lebanese officials revise displacement figure to 1.6 million (>25% of population). Lebanese MoPH cumulative reaches 2,679 killed / 8,229 wounded, with 20 killed and 46 wounded on 03 May alone. Codifies emergence of Lebanon as principal active theater; sets up 04 May escalation to first-class dashboard treatment.

Lebanon MoPH cumulative passes 2,696 killed / 8,264 wounded as IDF strikes 20+ Hezbollah sites: Lebanese MoPH (via NNA): 2,696 killed, 8,264 wounded since 2 March (+37 killed, +81 wounded vs 03 May). IDF strikes Deir Siryan-Zawtar, Kounine (Bint Jbeil), Baraachit, Kafra, Jannata, Deir Qanoun al-Nahr, Kharayeb (Zahrani). Netanyahu (at IDF senior command conference 04 May): 'We are striking now — in the security zone, north of the security zone, and north of the Litani… We are on the way to disarming Hezbollah… [Hezbollah] has about 10% of the missiles it had at the beginning of the war.' Two missions remain. Lebanese President Aoun: cited Litani-bridge strikes as 'prelude to ground invasion.' Lebanese-Israeli talks (Israel-requested 2-3 week deadline) deteriorating. Confirms Lebanon as principal active kinetic theater.

Lebanese MoPH cumulative toll surpasses 2,700 killed / 8,311 wounded since 2 March: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health reports cumulative casualties have exceeded 2,700 killed and 8,311 wounded. UNHCR notes 380 Lebanese killed since the April 17 Israel-Lebanon ceasefire 'took effect' — i.e., post-ceasefire violations remain at scale. Despite formal ceasefire, IDF strikes have continued daily in southern Lebanon and the Beqaa Valley.
Strait of Hormuz off Dubai: Cruise missile (per CBS citing US officials) — Several crew injured, evacuated for medical care

Israel breaks Lebanon ceasefire — IDF strike on Beirut Dahiyeh kills Hezbollah Radwan commander Ballout: Israeli airstrike on southern Beirut suburbs (Haret Hreik / Ghobeiri) killed Ahmed Ghaleb Ballout (also rendered Malek Ballout per AFP/Hezbollah-adjacent), Operations Commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force, plus Nasr regional intel chief Muhammad Ali Bazi and Aerial Defense Chief Hussein Hassan per IDF. First Beirut strike since the April 17 Lebanon ceasefire. PM Netanyahu/DM Katz announced action; coordinated in advance with US (per Israeli source to CNN). 11+ killed in concurrent strikes across south/east Lebanon May 6-7. IDF says 220+ Hezbollah killed in past few weeks (85 in past week). Lebanese MoPH cumulative since Mar 2: 2,727 killed / 8,438 wounded (CNN/MoPH May 7; +31/+174 since May 4).

WHO: 152 attacks on healthcare in Lebanon, 103 deaths, 241 injuries since conflict started: WHO Director-General Tedros (May 6 statement, surfaced May 7): 152 attacks on healthcare verified in Lebanon resulting in 103 deaths and 241 injuries since the conflict started; 3 hospitals + 41 primary health centers closed; 16 hospitals damaged. Lebanese MoPH cumulative since Mar 2: 2,727 killed / 8,438 wounded (CNN/MoPH May 7; +31 killed, +174 wounded since May 4 floor 2,696/8,264); 177 children killed.

Israel kills at least 24 in Lebanon Saturday; widest strike radius since Apr 17 ceasefire: Lebanese MoPH: 24+ killed across south Lebanon and Beirut–Sidon coastal highway including 7 in Saksakieh (1 child + 15 wounded), 3 in Saadiyat, 3 in Haboush, 3 in Nahrain, plus a Syrian father and his 12-year-old daughter killed in a triple-tap drone strike in Nabatieh. Hezbollah responded with multiple drone/rocket attacks on northern Israel and Misgav Am; 1 IDF reservist severely wounded, 2 moderately. Euronews (May 10) raised Saturday south-Lebanon toll to 39. Negotiations between Israel and Lebanon scheduled for May 14–15 in Washington despite Lebanese demand for cessation of strikes first.

WSJ: Israel ran secret airbase in Iraqi western desert during air campaign on Iran: Wall Street Journal reports IDF built a secret base in the Iraqi desert to support its Iran air campaign, and even struck Iraqi forces who came close to discovering it in early March (Iraq attributed those strikes to the US at the time). Baghdad has not yet officially responded. Material increase in scenario's intelligence-thread and US-Iraq relations risk.

IDF 91st Division strikes 40+ Hezbollah sites over weekend; Hezbollah hits Iron Dome battery with drone: IDF press service: 91st 'Galilee' Division struck 'more than 40 terror infrastructure sites and eliminated more than 10 Hezbollah terrorists' over the weekend in southern Lebanon (Worthy Christian News claims 'over 100 terrorists'; IDF official figure is 10+). Hezbollah released video showing drone strike on Iron Dome battery in northern Israel. Sirens sounded near Lebanon border. Lebanese MoPH: 36 killed in past 24h per Sunday count. IDF intercepted suspicious aerial targets in two separate Sunday incidents without triggering broader sirens.

Lebanon MoPH refreshed: 2,869 killed since Mar 2; 74 killed in last 3 days: Lebanese Ministry of Public Health, via Reuters/Detroit News, refreshed cumulative toll to 2,869 killed since March 2 (incl. 584 medics/women/minors); 74 killed in the last 3 days. UN reports ≥103 medical workers killed cumulative. President Aoun met US Ambassador Michel Issa May 11; urged US pressure on Israel to halt strikes and demolitions in south Lebanon. IDF spokesman Avichay Adraee issued evacuation orders for Deir al-Zahrani, Jarjouh, Sajjad (Jezzine district).

IDF orders evacuation of Deir al-Zahrani, Jarjouh, Sajjad (Jezzine district): IDF Arabic-language spokesman Avichay Adraee posted evacuation orders on X for the southern-Lebanon villages of Deir al-Zahrani, Jarjouh, and Sajjad (Jezzine district). Comes 24h after May 10 strikes killed 23 Lebanese including 2 Islamic Health Committee paramedics in Qalaway and Tibnin.

Southern Lebanon (multi-locale): Airstrikes across southern Lebanon — At least 19 killed, including four women and three children (Lebanon Health Ministry); cumulative Lebanese dead since March 2 exceeds 3,020. One IDF soldier — Sgt. Sapir — killed in combat in southern Lebanon, the 8th IDF soldier KIA since the April 16 ceasefire and the 21st since hostilities began.

Israeli strikes kill 8 in southern Lebanon, 3 women and 3 children among dead: Israeli airstrikes on Doueir, Tibnin, and Burj Shemali in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon killed 8 people, including 3 women and 3 children, per the Lebanon Health Ministry. The IDF said it struck 30+ Hezbollah targets. The cumulative Lebanese death toll since March 2 reached 3,073, with 9,362 wounded and more than 1.6M displaced.

Hezbollah losses: internal Hezbollah sources say 1,000+ fighters killed; IDF claims 1,700 killed.

+1 IDF KIA in southern Lebanon; PM Salam accuses Israel of 'scorched-earth policy': One additional IDF soldier (age 21) was killed in southern Lebanon May 30 in combat operations (four wounded). NPR (May 30) reported the Lebanese Health Ministry's running tally at ≥3,300 killed since the war began (~20% women, children, medics). UN peacekeepers said Israel launched 3,000+ strikes in southern Lebanon 'since last Sunday' versus 187 by Hezbollah and allies. Lebanese PM Nawaf Salam (May 30) accused Israel of pursuing a 'scorched-earth policy.'

Lebanese MoPH May 31: 3,412 killed / 10,269 wounded / 127 healthcare workers killed: The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health's May 31 bulletin recorded a cumulative tally of 3,412 killed, 10,269 wounded, and 127 healthcare workers killed since the Lebanon war began. The +112 daily delta versus Day 92's NPR-cited ≥3,300 baseline reflects continued intense Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon and the Beirut periphery across the weekend; UN peacekeepers had said Israel launched 3,000+ strikes 'since last Sunday' versus 187 by Hezbollah and allies.

Israeli strike near Tyre hospital; UN 'deeply alarmed,' WFP warns of emergency: An Israeli strike hit near a hospital in Tyre on June 1. The UN said it was 'deeply alarmed,' and the World Food Programme warned of a 'deepening humanitarian emergency' in Lebanon. The Lebanese Health Ministry's June 1 cumulative was reported at 3,355 killed; the June 2 bulletin recorded 3,433 killed / 10,395 wounded since March 2.

Lebanese MoPH June 2: 3,433 killed / 10,395 wounded: The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health's June 2 bulletin recorded a cumulative 3,433 killed and 10,395 wounded since the Lebanon war began on March 2 — up +21 killed and +126 wounded from the May 31 tally of 3,412 / 10,269, reflecting the intense June 1 fighting around Beaufort Castle, Dahiyeh, and Tyre. (A June 1 figure of 3,355 had circulated but sat below the May 31 bulletin and is flagged for reconciliation.)

Lebanon's deadliest post-MOU day: at least 47 killed, 4 IDF soldiers KIA: June 19 was the deadliest day on the Lebanon front since the MOU. Hezbollah struck an IDF tank near the Ali al-Taher hilltop overlooking Nabatieh, killing four Israeli soldiers, saying it was responding to Israeli ceasefire violations; Israel struck 'Hezbollah infrastructure' in Nabatieh, the Bekaa Valley (Douris) and elsewhere, and the Lebanese Health Ministry reported at least 47 killed (an earlier overnight count was 18). Netanyahu ordered the IDF to strike 'with full force.'

Israeli strikes kill at least 11 in south Lebanon — deadliest since the June framework: Israeli air strikes killed at least 11 and wounded 19 in southern Lebanon (7 killed at Ansar, including 3 children; 4 killed at Deir ez-Zahrani), the Lebanese Health Ministry said. Israel said it hit Hezbollah infrastructure in a 'security zone' after Hezbollah explosive-drone attacks along the Ali al-Taher ridge seriously wounded three Israeli troops. Hezbollah urged Beirut to abandon US-mediated talks and warned of an 'appropriate response'; President Aoun called the strikes a 'clear message' aimed at the negotiations. Cumulative Lebanon toll since Mar 2: at least ~4,300.

Iran infrastructure: 115,000+ civilian buildings damaged; 309 health facilities + 42 ambulances damaged (IRCS); 7 Iranian hospitals evacuated; 700+ educational facilities damaged, 30+ universities struck; 120+ historical sites reported damaged; partial power blackouts confirmed in Tehran and Karaj by Iran's energy minister; Pasteur Institute (Iran's premier public health facility, inoperable), Khatam-al-Anbia and Gandhi hospitals damaged; Delaram Sina Psychiatric Hospital, Tofigh Daru pharmaceutical, Shahid Mutahhari Hospital destroyed. Bushehr NPP: no new strikes Apr 16-17; Apr 4 projectile strike (4th incident) killed one physical-protection staffer and damaged an auxiliary building — no radiation increase. Iran submitted incidents via INFCIRC/1353 Apr 9. IAEA DG Grossi remains 'deeply concerned' and continues invoking the 'Seven Indispensable Pillars.' AEOI head Eslami refuses inspections of struck facilities pending codified protocols for 'internationally protected facilities subjected to military attacks.' Mahshahr Petrochemical Zone struck Apr 4 (5 killed, 170 injured). All Iranian ports blockaded since Apr 13; Iran's National Petrochemical Co suspended all petrochemical exports 'until further notice' Apr 15. ICRC delivered its first shipment into Iran Apr 14 — 171 metric tonnes via 14 trucks from Jordan, serving ~25,000 people (first since war start). Lebanon (Lebanese MoPH via WAFA/Al Jazeera Apr 17): 2,167-2,196 killed / 7,061 wounded; 172 children, 250+ women, 93 health workers killed. WHO Lebanon: 133 attacks on healthcare; 80+ health-worker deaths; 55 primary care centers and 6 hospitals closed; 14 hospitals damaged. OCHA Lebanon flash appeal seeks $308.3M through May. UNHCR reports 202,477+ cross-border flows from Lebanon into Syria since Mar 2 (incl. 27,343 Lebanese nationals). UNICEF Rapid Response Mechanism in Lebanon has reached 188,155 IDPs across 360+ shelters. Qaaqaiyet el Jisr and Delaffi bridges plus Litani crossings destroyed — isolating the south. 472 schools repurposed as shelters. Sultaniye power station damaged; water pipelines in Marjaayoun hit. Battle of Bint Jbeil: IDF 98th Division consolidated the sector — Apr 16 Egoz Unit raid on Hezbollah 'combat compound' in Aynata casbah seized RPGs, Kalashnikovs, grenades, an anti-aircraft missile, and surveillance gear; IDF demolished ~70 Hezbollah infrastructure sites in under a minute via coordinated detonation. Separately IDF recovered 130+ weapons stashed in a Bint Jbeil school alongside Hezbollah flags. Cumulative Bint Jbeil toll: 100+ Hezbollah fighters killed. IDF strike on Nabatieh Apr 16. Lebanon ceasefire effective 5:00 PM ET Apr 16; tens of thousands of IDPs began moving southward Apr 17 despite IDF spokesman Adraee's warning not to return south of the Litani yet. WHO Flash Appeal $30M for 5 most-affected countries (incl. $10M for Lebanon). WHO Lebanon mobilized 60+ tonnes of medical supplies since Mar 18 via EU Humanitarian Airbridge. Displacement: Lebanon >1.2M internal (~20% of population); Iran up to 3.2M IDPs (UNHCR Mar 12, likely stale); 4.4M Afghan refugees at elevated risk. Source: WHO / IRCS / IAEA / OCHA / UNHCR / HRANA / UNICEF / Hengaw / NBC News / Lebanese MoPH / WAFA / Al Jazeera / ICRC.
